children: It’s been an eventful weekend in the world of politics. From President
Donald Trump
’s reported use of AI in geopolitical discussions to legal battles, rising tensions with Iran and debates over AI data centers and taxes, here’s a quick look at the top stories that made headlines.
Trump, Musk And Grok: AI Enters Geopolitical Discussions
Trump reportedly sought insight from
Elon Musk
’s
Grok
chatbot about how Venezuelans might respond if President
Nicolas Maduro

were captured. The reported exchange took place weeks before the U.S. launched an operation that removed Maduro from power, adding another unusual dimension to the relationship between Trump, Musk and artificial intelligence.
Trump’s $10 Billion IRS Lawsuit Faces Another Legal Setback

A federal appeals court upheld a lower court’s finding that President Trump’s $10 billion lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service was improperly coordinated. The three-judge panel also upheld related sanctions against attorneys, leaving intact the lower court’s conclusion that the case lacked genuine adversity between Trump and the IRS.
Iran’s Supreme Leader Challenges U.S. As Trump Confirms Talks
Iran’s Supreme Leader
Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei

criticized the United States, saying Tehran’s opponents had suffered "painful blows" and would eventually be forced out of the Middle East. The comments came as Trump confirmed that talks were taking place through mediators, highlighting the contrast between Iran’s public statements and ongoing diplomatic contacts.
Read the full article here.
Trump Defends Ohio Data Centers Amid AI Power Cost Concerns

President Trump defended AI data centers during a rally in Ohio as concerns grow over their potential impact on electricity costs. Trump said the facilities could bring significant economic benefits to the state and argued that they could not simply be shut down because investment could move overseas.
Mike Johnson Attacks Democrats Over Tax Legislation

House Speaker Mike Johnson criticized House Democrats over their votes on tax legislation, accusing 212 Democrats of supporting what he called the "LARGEST TAX HIKE in history." Johnson also pointed to Democratic opposition to Republican-backed provisions involving tips, overtime and Social Security, underscoring the competing tax arguments from both parties.
